newsitem.title: USA: IMF releases $647.2 million in funds for Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF releases $647.2 million in funds for Russia.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Friday approved the resumption of lending to Russia, ordering the release of $647.2 million to the country as a result of tough action it took to revamp its struggling economy.

It said it approved the funding on the basis of the country achieving monetary and fiscal targets for last December, as well as the continued appropriate conduct of credit policy and efforts to improve tax collection.
The IMF board also cited "several important structural reform measures" as reason to release the funds, which are equal to roughly two monthly tranches under the program.
The IMF delayed payment of several tranches of a $10 billion standby loan agreement made between it and Russia last year, in part because the country had been slow to meet reform commitments.
It had stalled on making payments under the loan because tax revenues were well below budgeted levels, threatening to undermine government finances, according to monetary sources.
